# Algorithms, Games, and Economics

This course explores Algorithmic Game Theory, the intersection of computer science, game theory, and economics. It covers designing algorithms that perform well when agents act selfishly, with examples from auctions, resource allocation, and cryptocurrency markets such as Bitcoin. It also applies algorithmic perspectives to analyze economic markets, and may end with recent directions such as algorithmic lenses on behavioral or blockchain economics.

The `lecture-notes` skill (`shared/.github/skills/lecture-notes/SKILL.md`) has the full workflow for reading handwritten lecture notes.
